tEn: Robots That Predict the Future: Dyna-2 and Physical AI with Jason Ma
tZh: 预测未来的机器人：Dyna-2 与物理 AI——对话 Jason Ma
sEn: Jason Ma, co-founder and chief scientist of Dyna Robotics, explains how the Dyna-2 world action model predicts future video and robot actions to make physical AI more dexterous and generalizable.
sZh: Dyna Robotics 联合创始人兼首席科学家 Jason Ma 解析 Dyna-2 世界动作模型如何通过预测未来视频与机器人动作，让物理 AI 更灵巧、更具泛化能力。

consensus.en: World action models predict future video and actions, enabling dexterous, generalizable robot control.
consensus.zh: 世界动作模型预测未来视频和动作，实现灵巧、可泛化的机器人控制。

consensus.en: A generalist foundation model trained on massive human data can adapt to new tasks with minimal fine-tuning.
consensus.zh: 基于海量人类数据训练的通用基础模型，只需少量微调即可适应新任务。

consensus.en: Scaling data is key for robotics, but unlike language, there is no internet; data must be collected.
consensus.zh: 数据规模扩张是机器人技术的关键，但与语言不同，没有现成互联网数据，必须自行收集。

consensus.en: Deploying robots across many customer sites validates value and drives iterative improvement.
consensus.zh: 在众多客户站点部署机器人能验证价值并推动迭代改进。

consensus.en: Hardware and data are the main bottlenecks for general-purpose robots, not just model architecture.
consensus.zh: 硬件和数据是通用机器人的主要瓶颈，而不仅仅是模型架构。

consensus.en: An agentic harness with high-level reasoning and low-level action models enables long-horizon tasks.
consensus.zh: 结合高层推理和低层动作模型的智能体式框架，能实现长时程任务。

contrarian.en: Humanoid form factor is not optimal now; semi-humanoid with wheels is more practical and stable.
contrarian.zh: 人形形态目前并非最优；带轮子的半人形更实用、更稳定。

contrarian.en: Scaling laws apply to robotics, but the bitter lesson means simpler algorithms with right data beat handcrafted priors.
contrarian.zh: 缩放定律适用于机器人，但苦涩的教训意味着简单算法加正确数据胜过手工设计的先验。

contrarian.en: Synthetic data from frontier models and world models will be the next frontier for scaling robotics.
contrarian.zh: 来自前沿模型和世界模型的合成数据，将成为机器人规模扩张的下一个前沿。

contrarian.en: Owning the full stack, including hardware, is crucial; model-only approaches miss key bottlenecks.
contrarian.zh: 拥有包括硬件在内的全栈至关重要；仅做模型的方法会错过关键瓶颈。

contrarian.en: Vision-only world models may be insufficient; tactile and other modalities could be more data-efficient.
contrarian.zh: 仅视觉的世界模型可能不够；触觉和其他模态可能更具数据效率。

contrarian.en: Iterative semi-humanoid deployment yields faster progress than building a perfect humanoid for years.
contrarian.zh: 迭代式半人形部署比花数年打造完美人形能更快取得进展。

turns.en: All right, we're here on site with Jason Ma, co-founder and chief scientist of Dino Robotics. Thanks for having us in your...
turns.zh: 好的，我们来到了现场，和 Jason Ma 在一起，他是 Dino Robotics 的联合创始人兼首席科学家。感谢你让我们来到你的……

turns.en: Of course. Thank you for coming.
turns.zh: 当然。感谢你们能来。

turns.en: Yeah, it's been a blast. So, we got to see, you'll see a lot of B-roll, but we got to see drinks being pulled, a lot of evils, robots with knives for the first time. So, under the hood of all this, you have a world action model. What is that?
turns.zh: 是的，非常有趣。我们看到了，你们会看到很多 B-roll，但我们看到了饮料被拉出来，很多邪恶的东西，第一次看到机器人拿着刀。所以，在这一切的背后，你有一个世界行动模型。那是什么？

turns.en: Yeah, so last month we released our world action model called Dina 2. So, it's the first world action model trained on more than 1 million hours of data. So going back to your question first, world action model is a model that's able to predict the future video, the future state of the world. So hence the name world model. But in addition, you could also use that future generation to also produce actions robots can execute in the physical world to control the robot. So why do we do that? It's a very powerful architecture because if you think about how humans act in the physical world in our brain, we are implicitly thinking about how the world will evolve based on our actions. So now we have a model architecture that's able to do that to guide robot actions. So what we find is that by doing so the model is much more dextrous, much more robust and much more capable of generalizing to environments to scenarios is never seen before.
turns.zh: 是的，上个月我们发布了我们的世界行动模型，叫做 Dina 2。所以，这是第一个在超过 100 万小时数据上训练的世界行动模型。所以先回到你的问题，世界行动模型是一个能够预测未来视频、世界未来状态的模型。因此得名世界模型。但此外，你也可以利用这种未来生成来产生机器人可以在物理世界中执行的动作，以控制机器人。那么我们为什么这样做？这是一个非常强大的架构，因为如果你想想人类在物理世界中大脑是如何行动的，我们隐含地思考世界将如何根据我们的行动演变。所以现在我们有一个模型架构能够做到这一点来指导机器人的行动。我们发现，通过这样做，模型更加灵巧，更加鲁棒，并且更能够泛化到从未见过的环境和场景。

turns.en: Yeah. I want to prompt this question a bit. I think a lot of people hear world model and they think you're outputting video or world or 3D state. Um you're also doing action. I think most people don't understand what models are under the hood of robotics. So what is input output? What's the training data? What is the architecture? Give us all the details.
turns.zh: 是的。我想稍微引导一下这个问题。我认为很多人听到世界模型，他们会认为你在输出视频或世界或 3D 状态。嗯，你也在做动作。我认为大多数人不理解机器人技术背后的模型是什么。那么输入输出是什么？训练数据是什么？架构是什么？给我们所有细节。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. So uh for inputs the most important input is video, right? You know, you can think about videos that the robot is capturing with its cameras, right? So video or images of the, you know, past many seconds. That's the input. But for robots, what's really interesting is that robot also has a lot of actuator, a lot of joint encoders on itself. So the robot also knows, you know, the angles of its joints. So those can also be inputs to these world model. That's something that's very different from just a pure video model that's only looking at videos, right? So that's the input. And additionally for robots you want to be able to talk to it to instruct it to do different tasks right. So you can also feed it like language instruction. So those are what I consider the basic set of inputs that go into any robotics models including world action models. And once we have that the output at the uh basic level it needs to output actions the robots can execute on the hardware. But in the case of world action model, what's really interesting is that in addition to the actions, you can also output future video, right? So basically you can almost output the future video or some representation of it first and then use that to guide robot actions. So the way I think about is like this is kind of analogous to you know chain of thought you know basically the robots the models are reasoning in the visual the physics space and then outputting actions. So that's the key difference between world action models outputs versus other kind of models, robot models outputs.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。所以嗯对于输入，最重要的输入是视频，对吧？你知道，你可以想想机器人用摄像头捕捉的视频，对吧？所以过去很多秒的视频或图像。这就是输入。但对于机器人来说，真正有趣的是机器人本身也有很多执行器，很多关节编码器。所以机器人也知道，你知道，它的关节角度。所以这些也可以作为这些世界模型的输入。这与仅仅看视频的纯视频模型非常不同，对吧？所以这就是输入。此外，对于机器人，你希望能够与它交谈，指示它做不同的任务，对吧？所以你也可以喂给它语言指令。所以这些是我认为进入任何机器人模型（包括世界行动模型）的基本输入集。一旦我们有了这些，输出在基本层面上需要输出机器人可以在硬件上执行的动作。但在世界行动模型的情况下，真正有趣的是，除了动作，你还可以输出未来视频，对吧？所以基本上你可以先输出未来视频或它的某种表示，然后用它来指导机器人的行动。所以我的思考方式是，这有点类似于你知道思维链，你知道基本上机器人，模型在视觉、物理空间中进行推理，然后输出动作。所以这就是世界行动模型输出与其他类型的模型、机器人模型输出之间的关键区别。

turns.en: Um you put out a good blog post around your model. I think a lot of people understand language models or transformers next token predictors. In this case you shared quite a bit. There's like diffusion flow matching. You're predicting next world state plus action. Um one thing you say is a million hours. How do you determine the architecture? Like what are the choices there? What is the architecture? I feel like in language models there's a lot of take something off the shelf, take trillions of tokens, do prediction SFT, RL and you have a model. What about this? How do you go from nothing to your model? Is there vanilla architecture off the shelf? Do you determine all this and what's what is the current state?
turns.zh: 嗯，你发布了一篇关于你模型的好博文。我认为很多人理解语言模型或 Transformer 的下一个词预测器。在这种情况下，你分享了不少。有像扩散流匹配。你在预测下一个世界状态加动作。嗯，你说的一件事是 100 万小时。你如何确定架构？比如那里有什么选择？架构是什么？我觉得在语言模型中，有很多是拿现成的东西，拿数万亿个 token，做预测 SFT、RL，然后你就有了一个模型。这个呢？你如何从零到你的模型？有现成的 vanilla 架构吗？你决定所有这些吗？当前状态是什么？

turns.en: Yeah, I think yeah, so the mental framework to think about how do we build models for robotics is that there are essentially a couple things to look at. one's data and the second is like how do we make a model learn as much as possible from that data. So let's first talk about the model actually right. So the blog post we released is our D2 word action model. So under the hood it's a diffusion transformer. So transformer is essentially like the language model you know uh uh sequence sequence match decoder only. Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为是的，所以思考我们如何为机器人构建模型的思维框架是，基本上有几件事要看。一是数据，第二是我们如何让模型尽可能多地从数据中学习。所以让我们先谈谈模型，对吧。所以我们发布的博文是我们的 D2 世界行动模型。所以底层是一个扩散 Transformer。所以 Transformer 本质上就像语言模型，你知道，嗯嗯序列序列匹配仅解码器。是的。

turns.en: But what's really interesting is that in visual domains, if you think about generating images, generating videos, and in this case robots looking at images to generate actions, people have found the diffusion kind of architecture to work really well. So what is a diffusion model? A diffusion model is a model that takes some random noise and through iterative computation can go from noise to something that's really high-dimensional, something really highly defined and with very fine-grained features. If you think about generating images, you want sharp edges, sharp corners, color contrast. And for robotics, even though you're not generating images, you're generating actions that need to be very precise, very smooth. So it has kind of the same consideration as generating images. So that's why from first principles, the whole field—not just us—has been using this kind of diffusion transformer architecture to train robotics foundation models. You need the transformer aspect because transformer is the thing that can just ingest the most amount of data and learn. Then diffusion helps you refine the outcome to get the smooth, precise, fine-grained motion you need to actually execute on the robot. So that's the architecture that goes behind a lot of our recent breakthroughs.
turns.zh: 但真正有趣的是，在视觉领域，如果你想想生成图像、生成视频，以及在这个案例中机器人通过看图像来生成动作，人们发现扩散类架构效果非常好。那么什么是扩散模型？扩散模型是一种接收随机噪声，并通过迭代计算从噪声变成非常高维、非常清晰、具有非常细粒度特征的东西的模型。如果你想想生成图像，你想要锐利的边缘、锐利的角、色彩对比。而对于机器人，即使你不是在生成图像，你是在生成需要非常精确、非常平滑的动作，它也有和生成图像类似的考量。所以这就是为什么从第一性原理出发，整个领域——不只是我们——一直在用这种扩散 Transformer 架构来训练机器人基础模型。你需要 Transformer 的部分，因为 Transformer 是能够摄入最多数据并学习的东西。然后扩散帮助你细化输出，得到你在机器人上实际执行所需的平滑、精确、细粒度动作。这就是我们最近很多突破背后的架构。

turns.en: And we've covered flow matching before on the podcast. It is mostly an efficiency speed-up. Like let's say you normally would take 40 to 100 diffusion steps, you can reduce it to four.
turns.zh: 我们在播客里之前讲过流匹配。它主要是一种效率上的加速。比如说你通常需要 40 到 100 个扩散步骤，你可以把它减少到四步。

turns.en: Yeah, that's right. So with a diffusion model, one thing that's really hard in practice is that you need to tune the scheduler—like by how much you're converting the initial noise input into the final output. So flow matching is kind of like a special case of diffusion that makes the transformation much simpler. In practice, you don't have to tune as much and it works just as well. That is why I think about two to three years ago, most generative modeling for image and video has shifted from a diffusion model to a flow matching model. But the concept is the same, and flow matching is just a special, simpler-to-tune variant of diffusion.
turns.zh: 是的，没错。对于扩散模型，实践中一件很难的事是你需要调调度器——比如你把初始噪声输入转换成最终输出的程度。所以流匹配有点像扩散的一个特例，让变换简单得多。实践中你不必调那么多，效果也一样好。这就是为什么我觉得大约两三年前，大多数图像和视频的生成建模已经从扩散模型转向流匹配模型。但概念是一样的，流匹配只是扩散的一个特殊、更容易调的变体。

turns.en: Yeah, it actually makes me think that so flow matching obviously has trade-offs in quality.
turns.zh: 是的，这其实让我想到，流匹配显然在质量上有取舍。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: But actually, it's very suited for action diffusion and robotics because you get to re-evaluate in real time.
turns.zh: 但实际上，它非常适合动作扩散和机器人，因为你可以实时重新评估。

turns.en: That's right.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: Whereas in images, it's basically one shot.
turns.zh: 而在图像里，基本上是一次性的。

turns.en: That's right.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: Which is pretty fun. We got to mess with the laundry folding robot like you know throw a random towel in. Um the models adapt, right?
turns.zh: 这挺有趣的。我们玩了叠衣服机器人，比如随便扔一条毛巾进去。模型会适应，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: I think one key thing about your models is that they're made to be generalist. So one foundation model and you adapt them a lot. How does that work? Basically in 45 minutes of mapped data you can generalize towards—we saw an example of pulling drinks out of a fridge. What's the mindset there of one general model and then how do you adapt to different tasks?
turns.zh: 我觉得你们模型的一个关键点是它们是通用型的。所以一个基础模型，然后你大量地适配它们。这是怎么运作的？基本上用 45 分钟的数据你就能泛化到——我们看到了一个从冰箱里拿饮料的例子。那里面的思路是什么，一个通用模型，然后你如何适配不同任务？

turns.en: Yeah. So the way we think about it is that for robotics we need to build a very general, strong base model, right? And then because if you think about how a human interacts and behaves in the physical world, we have very strong base knowledge, we can just readily do a lot of tasks. But if you want to become an expert at any given task, there's some amount of training that needs to happen. And I think to train a general-purpose robot like the one we're building here, the same principle has to apply. So our approach is to first train a general model that's trained on as much data as we can find. So that is when our Dino report—our model is trained over a million hours of human data as a starting point. And then given that strong foundation, what we found is we can quickly make the robot or make the model do many, many different tasks with a very minimal amount of fine-tuning, to just tell the model here's the task I wanted to do and here's a very few amount of demonstrations, and the model can readily do a bunch of the tasks that you have seen.
turns.zh: 是的。我们思考的方式是，对于机器人，我们需要构建一个非常通用、强大的基础模型，对吧？然后因为如果你想想人类在物理世界中如何互动和行为，我们有非常强的基础知识，可以随时做很多任务。但如果你想成为任何给定任务的专家，就需要一定量的训练。我认为要训练一个像我们在这里构建的通用机器人，同样的原则必须适用。所以我们的方法是先训练一个通用模型，用我们能找到的尽可能多的数据来训练。所以我们的 Dino 报告——我们的模型以超过一百万小时的人类数据作为起点进行训练。然后有了那个强大的基础，我们发现我们可以用非常少的微调快速让机器人或模型做许多许多不同的任务，只需告诉模型这是我想做的任务，这里只有很少量的演示，模型就能轻松完成你见过的一堆任务。

turns.en: We actually have quite a few people who deal in data, who sell data. What is good data? What is bad data? What do you want to buy?
turns.zh: 我们其实有不少做数据、卖数据的人。什么是好数据？什么是坏数据？你想买什么？

turns.en: Yeah. I think that these are all open questions. Obviously, I think the top important thing is egocentric data of humans doing tasks. What else would you modify on that basic statement?
turns.zh: 是的。我认为这些都是开放问题。显然，我认为最重要的事情是人类做任务的自我中心数据。在这个基本陈述上你还会修改什么？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Yeah. So I think data is the most important thing in robotics today because unlike language models, there is no internet, right? So every company that's building models, building hardware has to think about data. So there's roughly a couple different ways of operating here. One is that you can collect a lot of data yourself, which is what we are doing as well.
turns.zh: 是的。所以我认为数据是当今机器人领域最重要的事情，因为不像语言模型，没有互联网，对吧？所以每家构建模型、构建硬件的公司都必须考虑数据。这里大致有几种不同的运作方式。一种是你自己收集大量数据，这也是我们在做的。

turns.en: You have employees here doing that.
turns.zh: 你这里有员工在做这个。

turns.en: I mean, there are robots everywhere in the office, right? But if you think about how much data you need for a robotic foundation model, I think the amount of data any individual company can collect by themselves is just nowhere near sufficient, right? It's kind of like you're trying to build an internet by just having Reddit or just having Facebook. There are great websites, a lot of users, but it's not enough, right? So when we think about data, there has to be some sort of data acquisition happening, right? You buy data, you look at data that's already out there. And then there are many different tiers, right? You mentioned data quality. I think data quality in robotics is a non-stationary problem in the sense that what is high-quality data for your model changes over time. Like when your model doesn't know anything, when it's zero, any data is useful, right? You can use a lot of video data. In the case of egocentric data, I think it's actually a very good way of pre-training robots because human data is so diverse—it covers every single physical activity you can possibly imagine—and that gives the robot model such a strong prior on how the world can evolve around an embodied actor, a human. But the issue with human data is that before your robot looks exactly like a human, there's going to be some gap between human actions and robot actions. Right? turns.en: So the kind of recipe we're thinking about is: how do we take the largest source of data we have today, like egocentric data, to give the model a strong prior over everything physical manipulation can cover, and then combine that with a small amount of robotics data to make the robot master whatever task we're interested in. You really need to think about: this human data covers this part of robot cognition, I need robot data to cover the low-level reflex dexterity the robot also needs, and put them into one model. And I think that's what gives a really adaptable, really strong model at the end.

So, the model is not just like doing actions, it's also following language commands very faithfully and can also navigate back to you to fulfill the order. So, all right. So, got the right drink. It's going to nicely close the door and I think it's switching switching.
turns.zh: 所以这里，带有我们硬件的物理智能体将根据你在这个屏幕上选择的饮料为你拿一杯饮料。所以我们的研究人员，我和 Chad 负责这个项目，我们只是给你一个快速演示。所以在这种情况下，他们选择了香草奶昔饮料，机器人已经收到了命令。所以，它会去冰箱，然后现在使用世界动作模型 Dino 2 控制整个机器人为你拿到正确的饮料，然后取回它。这里真正有趣的是，这真的是为了展示智能体的能力。所以，模型不仅仅是在做动作，它也非常忠实地遵循语言命令，并且还可以导航回你身边来完成订单。所以，好的。所以，拿到了正确的饮料。它会很好地关上门，我认为它正在切换切换。

turns.zh: 是的。切换模式，因为这里是导航部分，我们可以让另一个高级推理模型来做，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah. So, this one has a reasoning layer and an action layer. So, it's a two model architecture. Underneath we are sending language prompts. Basically, a few sentence instruction to the reasoning model. And then the reasoning model is planning out what it needs to step by step. First go into the fridge and grab something and then come back and then hand it off to a human in sequence and oversee the whole execution. And the lower level action model is responsible for performing the manipulation and the dextrous task.
turns.zh: 是的。所以，这个有一个推理层和一个动作层。所以，这是一个双模型架构。在底层，我们向推理模型发送语言提示。基本上，是几句指令。然后推理模型会规划它需要一步步做什么。首先进入冰箱拿东西，然后回来，然后按顺序交给人类，并监督整个执行过程。而较低级别的动作模型负责执行操作和灵巧任务。

turns.en: Yeah. On the action model side, it also needs to be steerable. So you're telling it which of the six drinks you want to pick up. And then like our video action model sort of helps with imagining like understanding your intent. So you can imagine like what does it look like when this robot grabs a drink. And that sort of helps it really follow what you tell it to do. And then there's also some like timing aspects to this. It needs to recognize when you've grabbed the drink and then like release at exactly that point. And you don't want false positives. You don't want to drop a drink on the ground. So, there's all sorts of like little things you just have to be careful about to get a demo like this working.
turns.zh: 是的。在动作模型方面，它也需要是可操控的。所以你要告诉它你想拿起六种饮料中的哪一种。然后我们的视频动作模型有助于想象，比如理解你的意图。所以你可以想象这个机器人抓取饮料时是什么样子。这有助于它真正遵循你告诉它做的事情。然后还有一些时机方面的因素。它需要识别你何时抓取了饮料，然后在那个确切的时间点释放。你不想要误报。你不想要把饮料掉在地上。所以，要让这样的演示工作，有各种各样的小事情你必须小心。

turns.en: Yeah. And the model is quite good at this kind of dexterity and very robust. So, like Chad was saying, it's able to just recognize and kind of like imagine what it's going to look like if it grabs the right drink and then execute.

tldr.en: World action models predict future video and actions for dexterous robot control.
tldr.zh: 世界动作模型通过预测未来视频和动作，实现灵巧的机器人控制。

tldr.en: Robotics lacks internet data; scaling requires real-world collection and synthetic generation.
tldr.zh: 机器人领域缺乏互联网数据，扩展需要真实世界采集和合成生成。
